facts.fact: The Ministry of Health and Sanitation has rolled out the Malawi Health Care Information System (Mahis), a digital health records system meant to replace hard-copy health passport books, according to its director of quality management and digital health.
Mahis is in pilot phase at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital in Blantyre and at selected health centres nationwide; the number of health centres is not given.

The newspaper's check at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital's outpatient department found Mahis operational: registered patients no longer produced health passport books, and first-time patients had details captured at the registry and were issued a barcode; the ministry says each patient gets a unique identifier held on a server reachable by facilities through an interoperability layer.

Mahis was reported in pilot phase and live at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital's outpatient department on 3 September 2026, with the ministry hoping most health facilities will be digitised within the next year or so.
Mahis is under pilot at selected health centres nationwide alongside one central hospital; no count or share of health centres is stated.
